headline: Phillies drop opener in Washington, Wheeler up tonight
recap: The Phillies' most recent game was Tuesday's 6-3 loss at Washington. Alec Bohm's single scored Kyle Schwarber in the first, but the Nationals answered in the bottom half: Yohandy Morales's RBI double brought home Brady House, and Jorbit Vivas's single scored Morales, putting Washington ahead 2-1. Luis Arraez's RBI double scored Trea Turner in the third to tie it at 2-2. Kyle Schwarber's solo homer, his 45th, put Philadelphia back in front 3-2 in the fifth, but Andrés Chaparro answered with a solo homer of his own in the bottom of the inning to tie it 3-3. Washington broke it open in the seventh: with two runners on, Daylen Lile's three-run homer, his 21st, made it 6-3, the final score. Cristopher Sánchez started and took the loss, allowing five runs over 6.1 innings; Jonathan Bowlan surrendered the decisive homer to Lile in relief. Richard Lovelady picked up the win and Erik Tolman closed it out for his third save.
The Phillies are 83-68, second in the NL East, 5.5 games behind the division-leading Braves, and have lost one straight.

Philadelphia is at Washington again today for game two of the series at Nationals Park, with first pitch scheduled for 6:45 PM ET. Zack Wheeler starts for the Phillies opposite Jared Simpson for the Nationals; DraftKings lists the Phillies as -196 favorites.
